audit.whatIsWrong: The entry repeatedly describes a 'three-stack Q knockup' (wants.foe[0], spikes[1], mid, whys[2], full tldr, dosFull[2].t, dontsFull[0].t, report[0].t, report[11].t). Ntofo Strikes takes TWO stacks, and the payoff is a shockwave that PULLS enemies in — the opposite direction from a knockup.
audit.why: Riot's own text: 'On hit, grants a stack of Ntofo Strikes. At 2 stacks, K'Sante fires a shockwave that pulls enemies in.' The direction matters more than the count for a Trundle player: a knockup would eject him from Frozen Domain, but a pull drags him toward K'Sante, which is a different read on whether to keep fighting. Counting to three also means the player eats the second-stack payoff every time.
audit.corrected: Ntofo Strikes at two stacks fires a shockwave that pulls you in — count two, not three, and expect to be dragged toward him, not away.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'W AllOut' is used as an ability name in wants.foe[1], spikes[1], early, mid, whys[1] and dontsFull[2].t, and it is described as a block that negates the Chomp-empowered auto. Two errors in one: All Out is his R, his W is Path Maker, and Path Maker is not a block.
audit.why: Path Maker is a charge-up during which he takes reduced damage, then a dash that knocks back and stuns. It does not selectively negate one auto-attack, so 'time your Q to land while his W is on cooldown' is advice built on a mechanic that does not exist. What actually punishes the player is charging through his trade damage and ending the exchange with a stun. Path Maker is 14/13/12/11/10 and also carries true damage, so armour is not the answer to it.
audit.corrected: Path Maker (W, 14s at rank 1) charges with damage reduction, then dashes for a knockback stun — trade while it is on cooldown, and do not expect armour to blunt it.
sources: champ-data/_kits/ksante.json (W Path Maker, cd 14/13/12/11/10, trueDamage; R All Out)

audit.whatIsWrong: The entry builds an escape plan around Pillar of Ice against All Out — 'Use Pillar of Ice to interrupt his R isolation attempt', 'your Pillar must be up as a backup escape route before he ever looks to R', full phases[2].why 'between you and All Out to break his pattern'. Nothing anywhere says All Out ignores walls.
audit.why: Riot's text for All Out: 'K'Sante knocks an enemy back, launching them through any wall in their path.' A Pillar of Ice is a wall. The single most repeated piece of advice in this entry is therefore the one that gets the player killed: they hold a 21-second cooldown for a displacement that goes straight through it.
audit.corrected: All Out launches you through any wall in its path, your own Pillar of Ice included. Spend Pillar on his walk-up and his Footwork angle instead, and treat the R as unpreventable.
sources: champ-data/_kits/ksante.json (R All Out: 'launching them through any wall in their path')
champ-data/_kits/trundle.json (E Pillar of Ice, impassable terrain, cd 21/19.5/18/16.5/15)

audit.whatIsWrong: 'His percent-HP passive' appears in early, mid, late, whys[3] and whys[5], and spikes[2] calls it a 'percent-current-HP passive' that scales with stacked HP.
audit.why: Dauntless Instinct is not a percent-health passive. Riot: 'K'Sante's Abilities mark targets to take more damage on his next Attack. When All Out, K'Sante deals more damage with all Attacks and Abilities.' It is an ability-into-auto damage amp, which is a completely different tell — the player should be watching for an ability landing on them and stepping out of auto range, not counting trade length. Worse, the invented passive is used to argue his HP stacking hurts Trundle, when Subjugate steals a percentage of the target's Health: his HP pile is Trundle's payday.
audit.corrected: Dauntless Instinct marks you after any of his abilities so his next attack hits harder — the ability is the tell for the auto. And every point of HP he stacks is HP Subjugate takes a percentage of.

audit.whatIsWrong: Both ultimates are treated as independent timers — 'Track All Out before every commit', 'the only loss condition left is fighting with Subjugate down' — with no cooldown attached to either, and spikes[3]/whys[0] credit Chomp with an 'AS steal' it does not have.
audit.why: All Out and Subjugate are both 120/100/80. They come up on the same timer at every rank, so the level-6 spike is genuinely shared and the trade is decided by who commits second, not by out-waiting him. Chomp steals Attack Damage, not attack speed — the attack speed in this matchup comes from Frozen Domain, which is a separate 18/17/16/15/14 cooldown.
audit.corrected: All Out 120/100/80 against Subjugate 120/100/80 — identical at every rank, so there is no window where yours is up and his is not. Chomp saps Attack Damage; the attack speed is Frozen Domain's.
sources: champ-data/_kits/trundle.json (R cd 120/100/80; Q 'sapping some of their Attack Damage'; W cd 18/17/16/15/14)

audit.why: The entry's best original insight holds up and is worth keeping and sharpening: All Out costs him defences on purpose ('gaining increased damage, healing, and transformed abilities at the cost of reduced defenses'), so Subjugate — which takes Health, Armor and MR and doubles the theft over 4 seconds — pays out far less once he has pressed it. The correct sequencing is to steal first, then fight, which the entry gestures at but never states as an order.
audit.corrected: Subjugate him before he presses All Out — the resists he sheds on purpose are resists you cannot take.
sources: champ-data/_kits/ksante.json (R All Out: 'at the cost of reduced defenses')
champ-data/_kits/trundle.json (R Subjugate: Health, Armor and MR, doubled over 4s)

audit.whatIsWrong: The chart contradicts its own prose at Level 6. win[4] and phases[4].side both read Trundle, but whys[4] under that same stage says 'if he Rs and your Pillar is down, you have no answer' and the mid breakdown says 'At 6 his R is the danger'. The chart also sits oddly against the packet's 51.16% over 215 games while MC_WR_TABLES.trundle.ksante reads 41.45.
audit.why: A stage cannot be handed to Trundle and then justified with a sentence about having no answer. With both ultimates on 120/100/80 and All Out shedding the exact resists Subjugate wants, Level 6 is the most genuinely coin-flip stage in the lane — 'Skill' is the honest label. I have rewritten the whys so the reasoning at least stops arguing against its own side, but left the enum alone.
audit.corrected: Level 6 is a shared spike, not Trundle's: same 120/100/80 timer on both ultimates, and whoever commits second wins. win[4] and phases[4].side should read Skill.

audit.whatIsWrong: The content layer never mentions anti-heal, although the full layer already buys Executioner's Calling on the first back.
audit.why: All Out grants him increased healing for its whole duration, and it is the only phase of the matchup where he genuinely out-sustains Trundle. The two layers should not disagree about whether Grievous Wounds is core.
audit.corrected: Buy Grievous Wounds before you take the post-6 duel — All Out heals him for the whole duration.

From level 2 Path Maker changes the maths: he charges it taking reduced damage, so your trade lands into the cut, and the dash out knocks you back and stuns. edits.before: From levels 4 through 6 K'Sante controls the lane. His three-stack Q knockup is reliable enough to interrupt Frozen Domain every extended trade, and his W block means you cannot guarantee the Chomp AD steal lands when it matters most. You can still contest short trades — Q in, Chomp once or twice, Pillar to slow his chase and back out — but you cannot commit to the full Frozen Domain brawl he will interrupt. At 6 his R is the danger: it strips his own resistances on purpose, which cuts Subjugate's payoff significantly — you steal armor and MR he has voluntarily shed — and the isolation zone means your Pillar must be up as a backup escape route before he ever looks to R. If your Pillar is on cooldown and he Rs, you are fighting a fighter with no resistance-drain payoff and no knockup of your own to bail you out.
edits.after: From levels 4 through 6 K'Sante controls the lane. His two-stack Ntofo shockwave pulls you off Frozen Domain in every extended trade, and Path Maker lets him charge through your damage and close the exchange with a knockback stun. You can still take short trades — Chomp on its 3.5s, Pillar to slow the chase, walk out — but never the full domain brawl he can break. At 6 All Out is the danger: it strips his own resistances on purpose, so Subjugate pays out on stats he has voluntarily shed. Steal them before he presses it, not after. Do not plan Pillar of Ice as the escape either — All Out launches you through any wall in its path, your own pillar included. Both ultimates run 120/100/80, so the two windows open together and whoever commits second wins the fight.

edits.before: At two items the lane evens out because K'Sante is stacking HP and resistances again through Heartsteel and tank itemization, which does restore some Subjugate value — but his percent-HP passive and sustained dueling tools keep him competitive in the 1v1. Your best late-game angle is team fights: Subjugate a tanky frontliner who is NOT actively using R, Frozen Domain in the middle of the brawl, and Pillar to peel or to wall off their backline. Avoid the straight 1v1 if he has R available and your Pillar is down — the isolation removes your ability to kite out, and your win condition at this stage is draining a tank who cannot shed their own stats to counter you.
edits.after: At two items the lane evens out because K'Sante is stacking HP and resistances again through Heartsteel and tank items — and that restores Subjugate's payout, which takes a percentage of Health, Armor and MR and doubles the theft across four seconds. Your best late angle is still team fights: Subjugate a frontliner who is not currently All Out, Frozen Domain in the middle of the brawl, and Pillar to peel or wall off their backline. Buy Grievous Wounds before you take the straight duel — All Out heals him for its whole duration. And do not bank on Pillar for the exit: his knock-back goes through any wall in its path.

notes: BIGGEST CORRECTION: the entry's most-repeated instruction was to hold Pillar of Ice as the answer to All Out. Riot's own text says All Out launches the target 'through any wall in their path' — a pillar does not stop it, so the player was being told to bank a 21-second cooldown for a displacement it cannot prevent. Second: 'three-stack Q knockup' is wrong twice over — Ntofo Strikes pays out at TWO stacks and it pulls, not knocks up, which changes both the count and the direction the player expects to travel. Third: 'W AllOut' conflated his W (Path Maker) with his R (All Out) and invented a per-auto block; Path Maker is a damage-reduced charge into a knockback stun on 14s at rank 1. Fourth: the 'percent-HP passive' does not exist — Dauntless Instinct is an ability-into-attack damage amp, and the invented version was used to argue his HP stacking devalues Subjugate when the opposite is true. Also added the shared 120/100/80 on both ultimates, which turns 'track his R' into a concrete symmetric read. UNVERIFIED, LEFT ALONE: whether Ntofo Strikes' pull can be spell-shielded or cleansed, and whether the pull interrupts Frozen Domain's benefits or merely moves you off the zone — the kit file's needsResearch block is empty for both champions, so I described the displacement only. WIN-RATE CONFLICT: packets/trundle.json gives 51.16% over 215 games; MC_WR_TABLES.trundle.ksante in champ-data/content/trundle.js reads 41.45. Those are ten points apart and I did not edit the table. NOT EDITED (enum): win[4] and phases[4].side read Trundle at Level 6 while whys[4] and the mid breakdown both argue the stage is dangerous for Trundle — with both ultimates on the same timer, 'Skill' is the honest value.
